releases.title: Progress while tests run

highlights.text: Running tests now shows a progress bar: what is loading, which test is running (Test 3 of 8), the seconds so far and when the run will be stopped.
The same indicator appears in lesson and math labs, coding and SQL problems, and the Playground.

notes: Screen readers hear each step once, not every second.
With reduced motion on, the bar stays still.

releases.title: Math for AI and ML plan

highlights.text: New study plan: 6 weeks of math for AI and ML at 6–8 hours a week: linear algebra, probability, statistics, calculus and optimisation.
25 hands-on Python labs that check themselves in the browser with NumPy, from vector norms to backpropagation and a numerically stable cross-entropy.
The Playground can now import NumPy in Python, offline once it has loaded.

notes: Passing a lab ticks its item in the plan.
NumPy ships with the app and is never fetched from a package index.

releases.title: Forward Deployed Engineer plan

highlights.text: New study plan: 8 weeks for Forward Deployed Engineer interviews, in Python or TypeScript, with an LLM apps or data integration track for weeks 6–7.
Five new Field Guide entries on customer engineering: discovery and scoping, case interviews, messy data, rapid prototypes and on-site debugging.
New coding problem: clean a messy customer export and keep the latest record per customer.

notes: Mock scorecards gain a Customer case kind: problem framing, decomposition, technical depth and communication.
Home shows today's tasks for every plan you have started.

releases.title: TypeScript in study plans

highlights.text: Study plans now let you pick TypeScript as your interview language. Python stays the default.
Coding problems can be solved in TypeScript, with a starter typed from the tests.
Plan links open problems and the Playground in your chosen language.

notes: The plan shows idioms for your language, a link to its track, and a short tip for each of weeks 1–7.
Type errors are listed but don’t fail tests. The TypeScript compiler downloads the first time you run TypeScript.
A TypeScript solve counts as a JavaScript solve. Your language choice is saved with plan progress and goes into backups.

releases.title: Pattern pictures on problems

highlights.text: Coding problems now show the picture from their pattern page once you reveal the first hint.
Each picture links back to its full pattern page, with the step-through, template and exercise.

notes: The picture stays hidden until you ask for a hint, so you can try the problem cold first.
It uses the same diagram as the pattern page, so themes, dark mode, high contrast and the text description all work the same.

releases.title: Study plans

highlights.text: New: Study plans. Follow a fixed week-by-week schedule with a daily checklist that links straight to the work.
The first plan: 10 weeks for Applied AI or ML engineer roles, with phase checks, an error log and mock scorecards.
Three new design cases: a RAG document copilot, a support agent with tools, and a recommendation system.

notes: Find Study plans under Me in the navigation, on the site map and with Ctrl+K, which also finds each week.
Pick a start date to get a Today card on the plan and on Home. Weeks 8–10 switch between the Applied AI and ML engineer tracks.
Phase checks are a soft gate: you can always work ahead, with a reminder to revisit your misses first.
Plan progress stays on this device and goes into backups. Older backups import exactly as before.

releases.title: Quieter updates and What’s new

highlights.text: Updates now download quietly and apply the next time you open DevPREP. No more reload banner.
Want it now? Relaunch now saves your work first and brings you back to the same page.
This changelog: see what changed in every release, searchable with Ctrl+K.

notes: A verified update waits until every DevPREP window is closed, then starts on the next launch. Your open windows are never reloaded for you.

Relaunch now (in App & offline at the bottom of every page) saves and rechecks your progress, drafts and Playground snippets first. It stops if saving is blocked and warns you if a timed mock or practice run is in progress.
With several windows open, relaunching one window offers a relaunch in the others instead of reloading them.
After an update, a short What’s new card appears once. Brand-new installs don’t see it.
The version you last saw is a local preference on this device. It is not part of progress backups.

releases.title: Playground

highlights.text: A Playground to write and run JavaScript, TypeScript, Python and SQL, with saved snippets.
Practise SQL on a persistent sandbox database with an optional sample schema.

notes: Snippets autosave on this device and are included in backups.
Run with Ctrl/Cmd+Enter. Python and JavaScript can read from a stdin box.
Works offline: Python and Postgres are cached after their first use.
Open in Playground copies your current code from a problem or lesson.

releases.title: Command palette and site map

highlights.text: Press Ctrl+K (⌘K on Mac) to search every lesson, problem, pattern, guide, case and company.
A site map shows every page in one place.

notes: Search is fuzzy, grouped by type, keyboard navigable and works offline.
Recent searches are remembered on this device.

releases.title: Navigation redesign

highlights.text: Five goal-based groups: Learn, Practise, Design, Interview and Me.
A tree sidebar on desktop and a bottom bar on phones, with breadcrumbs on every page.

notes: The sidebar tree goes down to individual items, shows progress marks and remembers what you expanded.
On phones, tapping a group opens its pages as a sheet.
Old bookmarks such as #today and #roadmap still work.

releases.title: Company prep

highlights.text: Company prep pages for big tech interviews: process, reported focus areas and a practice set.
Timed company mock loops that follow each company’s interview format.

notes: Interview processes are summarised from official careers pages, with sources and an “as of” date.
Behavioural prompts and STAR notes are stored on this device.
Company progress earns XP and badges and is included in backups.

releases.title: Whiteboard

highlights.text: A whiteboard for system design, with timed practice against a design case.
A scratchpad on coding problems for tracing arrays, trees and pointers.

notes: Boards are saved in this browser and can be exported as PNG or .excalidraw files.
A stencil library includes load balancers, caches, queues, databases and more.
Backups can include or leave out whiteboards.

releases.title: Patterns

highlights.text: A visual course on algorithm patterns, with step-through diagrams and a code runner.
Not sure which pattern fits? Try the pattern picker quiz.

notes: Each pattern page covers how to recognise it, a template in three languages, complexity and common mistakes.
A printable cheat sheet summarises every pattern.

releases.title: CodeMirror editor

highlights.text: A rich code editor with syntax highlighting, auto-indent and bracket matching.
Choose the rich or plain editor, and turn on interview mode, in Settings.

notes: Interview mode turns off autocomplete so practice feels like a real interview.
The plain editor remains available for screen readers and slower devices.
